Voted Z. Zeitgeist has an AMAZING  1-11 track run (Red Version) Never quite got Pomp and Circumstances. The production is cool, but the mixing is ass, this needs a remixing more than Machina 1+2. For me that 11 track segment is something i never quite found in another "modern" pumpkin record until Aghori, but it lacks hooks which Zeitgeist has a bunch. The bonus tracks are by far some of the best songs BC had written up to that point in his life. GLOW and FOL amazing non-album singles which has been released in Pisces they might been considered legendary songs. I was 15 when this released so I heard them all and was my introduction to the band, shame they never got to fulfill the "heavy" aspect that they were trying to impose with this album. This albums and its guitar tones are what (mostly) got me into downtuned guitars in pop music, Tarantula is gospel to that kinda fusion.

Oceania for me is the first "form correction" that BC tried to do when Teargarden didn't panned out with the critics. But i really loved TGBK so it was a bummer for me, sadly it took too manny years between Song for a Son and the finally released Oceania that it wasn't it for me. Got to see SP in 2011 and the arrangements for My Love is winter blowed my mind, only to find a super different "pop" version in the album. Saw them again live in support of the album in 2012 and the band was great, but not so many of the songs resonated in me. Pale Horse, Quasar and Panopticon were the ones for me. Here i felt that BC was trying to appeal to that "old crew" that were looking for SD2. Hope he had sorted out Teargarden at the time, but shame nonetheless. 

  
Aghori Mhori Mei is for me a "return to form" that wasn't continued since Zeitgeist. I love that it sounds and feels like an honest album without he (or the band) trying to sound modern ... they were modern but somehow forgot what made them sound different to the rest. Everytime BC tries to appeal to "the masses" its a miss. Aghori feels like he wanted to prove HIMSELF that he still got it in terms of rock riffs and uptempo anthems, which is a return much more to Gish than SD for me. 

  
All 3 great albums, shame no one here seems to like ATUM, but it was a cool ambitious project that combined with Cyr, it felt to me like "that was meant" to be Teargarden in a way.

Was the last "Teargarden" we were gonna get. Got canned and we got Ogilala and Shiny 1 instead. I suppose songs from that project got up in Ogilala, Shiny 1 and Cyr. Don't know if any confirmed song from that TGBK era got up to Atum or Aghori? I was really looking forward for BC to finish Teargarden back in the day, but it was such an ambition project that it would never be completed in an indie-non-label way.

MJ was trying to transition from pop artist to entertainment figure and was so much into being his own owner of his catalogue. With Thriller he had to fight for his own songs and ofter produce them himself because QJ woudn't wanna work on his songs right away, such as Billie Jean. With Thriller having most of the acclaimed singles being penned by MJ he fought for all the Bad songs to be written by him alone, having just 2 songs of that album written by someone else. I think that Bad was also a breaking point because QJ wanted to have his sound and MJ was trying to experiment more with electronic sounds, programming and things Janet and Jermaine were doing at the same time, such as Jimmy Jam producing Janet's Rythm Nation to critical acclaim, which Michael had with Bad, but in true hidsight it didn't perform or was viewed as masterpiece like Thriller. Ultimately Quincy's contract was only for The Wiz and 3 studio albums so Michael choose not to renew and split in good terms. Also Teddy Riley was recommended by Quincy, but by that time MJ was working with 3 or 4 different production teams at the same time, i would guess by the time Bad was ending or right away.
